known_defects: v2 carries the IPv6 limitation as a caption node with no edge: rataflow-view has no footnote/annotation field, so a stated limitation can only be drawn as a box. It is grouped `limit` and labeled as a limitation, but a reader can mistake it for a device.
`no committed rate` (a Part B answer in the source) is not drawn: the caption slot was spent on IPv6 and the v2 attempt budget (3) was used up. Disclosed, not silently dropped.

The router qualifier (`claimed`) appears in v3 but not in v2, where the same router box is labeled `Fios rtr 192.168.1.1`. Adding it to v2 produced 1 crossing (attempt 2), and crossings are kept at 0 by leaving the qualifier in the view that draws the interpreted ISP chain.

v2 draws the tailscale0 -> bond0 encapsulation as one edge that skips the host band. The renderer routes it in an outer corridor, which is honest but visually implies the packet bypasses the host; the host is the sender in both e5 and e6.
v3 is a single-file column: every node is in its own band, so it uses 37 of 47 rows and 31 of 77 columns. That is layout inefficiency, not clipping: extent 31x37 inside 77x47 at 100% zoom.
Static case: no view animates a dot, so `dots: 0 ... 0 synchronized`, `origins: 0/0` and a 5-frame static capture are the honest evidence. There is no motion claim to verify.
The `--check` runs report `viewport: unknown` when run headless; the measured size in the bundle comes from the app's own pane header `77x47 @100%` and the pane read.
